answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and as a result it pays the vault fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the copper ledger attributes every share, the zephyr audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 43% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 4 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
